A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AdaDetectGPT. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection AUCs, adversarial-attack evaluations, sensitivity studies, normality diagnostics and runtime measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical studies and additionally reports LRR results for the closed-source-model comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3(d) replaces the proposed maximum over multiple source-specific detector scores with detection using a single similar surrogate LLM. The central white-box witness statistic, spline-based fitting and normal-quantile threshold remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SQuAD, WritingPrompts, XSum, Yelp and Essay, plus PubMed in the adversarial experiments. The represented generation models, mixed human/machine passages and attack scenarios remain. Gemini results and adversarial evaluations are relocated, not newly introduced.

E2.justification: LRR is added to the GPT-4o, Claude-3.5 and Gemini-2.5 comparisons in v4 Tables 2 and S8. ImBD is removed from the runtime/memory comparison, although its accuracy results remain in Table S7.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix C.1 explicitly uses surrogate-generated text for black-box witness training, specifying the scoring model when surrogates differ. v4 Appendix C instead discusses target-model rewrites without establishing whether the reported training data changed. The main sample counts, prefix lengths, continuation limits and AUC metric remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The computational analysis loses its runtime/memory comparison against ImBD, retaining only AdaDetectGPT's scaling measurements. Sample-size and spline sensitivity, prompt-length distribution shifts, normality diagnostics and adversarial analyses otherwise remain; moving the attack table into the main text adds no new robustness evidence.

E5.justification: The variance-ratio means and variances and the KS/SW normality tests are retained unchanged, moving from Tables S4–S5 to S5–S6. No new seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: New LRR rows report average AUCs of 0.6243 for GPT-4o, 0.5723 for Claude-3.5 and 0.5906 for Gemini-2.5. ImBD runtime/memory entries are removed. Matched existing detector AUCs, attack results, diagnostic values and AdaDetectGPT timings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 removes the stochastic-dominance assumption and associated sharper-bound lemma, revises MCLT conditions and proof steps, and introduces a proportional-variance extension. New Appendix E.6 supplies smoothness-dependent estimation and TNR rates with a proof sketch. Appendix C also corrects the empirical objective's human/machine sign, and Appendix E.5 revises reciprocal-variance algebra.

C1.justification: The abstract reduces the headline improvement claim from 58% to 37%, and the introduction reduces the black-box claim from 58% to 20%. The principal contributions—adaptive witness learning, threshold selection and statistical guarantees—are retained.

C2.justification: The new Appendix E.3 remark argues that proportional variances can preserve the witness-learning rationale under weaker assumptions. The limitations discussion newly characterizes FNR control under sampling mismatch as conservative. The interpretation claiming greater computational efficiency than ImBD is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix C provides a more explicit approximation sequence, sample-variance construction, variance pooling and rewriting-based training explanation, and specifies random selection of two other training datasets. Model identifiers, generation prompts, baseline budgets, hardware and code-access disclosures are largely retained from v1's separate implementation appendices.

R1.justification: v4 adds the Yang et al. detection survey, Chen and Christensen's series-estimation work and several references supporting margin assumptions. It also mentions machine-revised-text detection explicitly. The overall positioning between statistical and machine-learning detectors remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix C is rewritten into a numbered derivation and incorporates the former experimental-details appendix. The experimental narrative, conclusion, limitations and author block are edited. These are localized revisions within the retained five-section main structure.

P2.justification: The Gemini table moves from main Table 3 to Appendix Table S8, while the adversarial table moves from S10 to main Table 3. Comparison rows and appendix caption placement change, and Figures S5 and S7 receive revised text styling while retaining their plotted findings.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects the sign inconsistency between Appendix C and the main objective, explains implementation more clearly, and supplies a proof sketch for the previously unelaborated smoothness-rate claim. These improve clarity and checkability. The gain is limited by largely unchanged empirical evidence, removal of the ImBD efficiency comparison and unresolved black-box training provenance.
